title.zh: 卷九十二 列傳第十七 杜闞王李苑羅王
title.en: Volume 92 Biographies 17: Du, Kan, Wang, Li, Yuan, Luo, Wang
title.raw: 卷九十二 列傳第十七 杜闞王李苑羅王 Volume 92 Biographies 17: Du, Kan, Wang, Li, Yuan, Luo, Wang

sentences.zh: 杜闞王李苑羅王

translations.literal: Du, Kan, Wang, Li, Yuan, Luo, Wang
translations.idiomatic: Du, Kan, Wang, Li, Yuan, Luo, and Wang

sentences.zh: 杜伏威，齊州章丘人。

translations.literal: Du Fuwei was a man of Zhangqiu in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei was a native of Zhangqiu in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 少豪蕩，不治生貲，與裏人輔公祏約刎頸交。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and unrestrained, did not manage his livelihood, and with a fellow townsman Fu Gongshi swore a friendship as close as cutting their throats together.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was wild and extravagant, paid no heed to making a living, and with a neighbor named Fu Gongshi he swore an oath of sworn brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 公礻石數盜姑家牧羊以饋伏威，縣跡捕急出《禮記·禮運》：「大道之行也，天下為公，選賢與能，講，乃相與亡命為盜，時年十六。

translations.literal: Gongshi repeatedly stole his aunt's sheep to give to Fuwei; when the county was urgently tracking them down, they together fled and became bandits, at age sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gongshi often stole sheep from his aunt's household to feed Fuwei. When the county authorities were hot on their trail, the two fled together and took to banditry. Fuwei was sixteen at the time.

sentences.zh: 伏威狡譎多算，每剽劫，眾用其策皆效。

translations.literal: Fuwei was cunning and full of stratagems; whenever they raided, the band used his plans and they always succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei was crafty and resourceful. On every raid his men followed his schemes, and they never failed.

sentences.zh: 嘗營護諸盜，出為導，入為殿，故其黨愛服，共推為主。

translations.literal: He once protected the other bandits on their raids—going out as guide and returning as rearguard—so his fellows admired and obeyed him, and together they made him their leader.
translations.idiomatic: He often shielded the other robbers on their raids, serving as vanguard on the way out and rearguard on the return, so his comrades admired and trusted him and together chose him as their chief.

sentences.zh: 隋大業九年，入長白山，依賊左君行，不得意，舍去，轉剽淮南，稱將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daye of Sui, he entered Mount Changbai, attached himself to the bandit Zuo Junxing, was dissatisfied, left, turned to plundering in Huainan, and called himself General.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Sui reign era Daye, he joined the bandits on Mount Changbai under Zuo Junxing. Finding no favor there, he left and turned to raiding in the Huai region, styling himself General.

sentences.zh: 下邳賊苗海潮擁眾鈔暴，伏威遣公祏脅諭曰：「天下共苦隋，豪桀相與興義，然力弱勢分不相統，若合以為強，則無事隋矣。

translations.literal: Miao Haichao of Xiapi had a crowd plundering; Fuwei sent Gongshi to coerce with words: "All under Heaven suffer together under Sui; heroes rise for righteousness, but forces are weak and divided without unified command. If we unite for strength, there will be nothing more to do with Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Haichao of Xiapi led a band that looted far and wide. Fuwei sent Fu Gongshi to intimidate him with a message: "The empire groans under the Sui; heroes everywhere are rising in revolt, yet their forces are weak and scattered and cannot act as one. If we join together we shall be strong enough to bring down the Sui.

sentences.zh: 公能為主，吾且從，不然，一戰以決。」

translations.literal: If you can be master, I will follow for the time being; otherwise we shall decide by one battle.
translations.idiomatic: If you will be our leader, I shall follow you for now; if not, let us settle it in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 海潮懼，即以眾下之。

translations.literal: Haichao was afraid and immediately submitted his followers to him.
translations.idiomatic: Haichao was frightened and at once placed his men under Fuwei's command.

sentences.zh: 江都留守遣校尉宋顥將兵捕擊，伏威與戰，偽北，誘顥墮葭榛澤中，順風縱火迫之，步騎燒死幾盡。

translations.literal: The Jiangdu garrison sent Colonel Song Hao with troops to pursue and strike; Fuwei fought him, feigned retreat, lured Hao into the reed marshes, sent fire with the wind against him, and nearly all his infantry and cavalry were burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangdu garrison commissioner sent Colonel Song Hao with troops to hunt him down. Fuwei gave battle, feigned a retreat, and lured Hao into a reed swamp; then, with the wind at his back, he set the reeds ablaze and drove the enemy into the flames until almost every foot soldier and horseman was burned alive.

sentences.zh: 海陵賊趙破陣聞伏威兵少，輕之，召使並力。

translations.literal: Zhao Pochen of Hailing heard Fuwei had few troops and despised him, summoning him to join forces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pochen, a bandit chief of Hailing, heard that Fuwei's force was small and held him in contempt, so he summoned Fuwei to join him.

sentences.zh: 伏威引親將十人操牛酒謁，勒公祏嚴兵待變。

translations.literal: Fuwei brought ten close commanders bearing oxen and wine to call on him, ordering Gongshi to keep troops ready for any change.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei took ten trusted officers carrying oxen and wine to pay a visit, while ordering Fu Gongshi to hold the army in readiness for any sudden move.

sentences.zh: 破陣引伏威入幕，置酒，悉召酋首高會。

translations.literal: Pochen led Fuwei into his tent, set out wine, and summoned all the chieftains to a grand gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Pochen brought Fuwei into his tent, set out wine, and called all the chieftains together for a great feast.

sentences.zh: 伏威突斬破陣，眾眙駭不及救，復殺數十人，下皆畏服，公祏兵亦至，遂並其眾，至數萬。

translations.literal: Fuwei suddenly struck and killed Pochen; the crowd stood stunned and could not rescue in time; he killed several tens more; all below were awed into submission; Gongshi's troops also arrived; he then absorbed their force, reaching tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei suddenly sprang up and slew Pochen. The assembly stood aghast and could not intervene in time. He killed several dozen more men, and all his subordinates submitted in fear. Fu Gongshi's troops arrived as well, and Fuwei absorbed Pochen's entire following, bringing his strength to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 攻安宜，屠之。

translations.literal: He attacked Anyi and slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Anyi and put the place to the sword.

sentences.zh: 隋遣虎牙郎將來整戰於黃花輪，伏威大敗，身重創，與公祏財有眾數百，亡去，行收卒得八千，與虎牙郎將公孫上哲戰鹽城，覆其軍。

translations.literal: Sui sent Tiger Tusk General Lai Zheng to battle at Huanghualun; Fuwei was badly defeated and badly wounded; he and Gongshi had only hundreds of followers and fled; as he went he gathered troops to eight thousand, fought Gongsun Shangzhe at Yancheng and destroyed his army.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui dispatched Tiger Tusk General Lai Zheng to fight him at Huanghualun. Fuwei suffered a crushing defeat and was gravely wounded. He and Fu Gongshi escaped with only a few hundred men, but as they marched they gathered troops until they had eight thousand, then met Tiger Tusk General Gongsun Shangzhe at Yancheng and annihilated his force.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣右禦衛將軍陳棱以精兵討之，棱不敢戰，伏威遺以婦人服，書稱陳姥，怒其軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent Right Imperial Guard General Chen Ling with elite troops to attack; Ling dared not fight; Fuwei sent him women's clothing with a letter addressing him as "Old Woman Chen," enraging his army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Right Imperial Guard General Chen Ling with picked troops against him. Ling would not give battle, so Fuwei sent him women's garments and a letter addressed to "Old Dame Chen," deliberately to humiliate him and stir his army to anger.

sentences.zh: 棱果悉兵至，伏威迎出挑戰，棱軍射中其額，伏威怒曰：「不殺汝，矢不拔！」

translations.literal: Ling indeed brought all his troops; Fuwei came out to challenge; Ling's army shot him in the forehead; Fuwei raged: "I will not pull out this arrow until I have killed you!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ling duly marched out with his full army. Fuwei rode forth to challenge him. Ling's archers struck Fuwei in the forehead. Fuwei roared, "I will not pull out this arrow until you are dead!

sentences.zh: 遂馳入棱陣，大呼沖擊，眾披靡，獲所射將，使拔箭已，斬之，攜其首入棱軍示之，又殺數十人，遂大潰，棱走而免。

translations.literal: He charged into Ling's formation shouting and attacking; the masses scattered; he seized the archer who had shot him, made him pull out the arrow, then beheaded him, carried the head into Ling's army to show it, killed several tens more, and the army broke utterly; Ling fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred straight into Chen Ling's ranks, shouting as he charged. The enemy lines crumbled. He seized the archer who had shot him, made the man draw out the arrow, then cut off his head and bore it into Ling's camp to display it. After killing several dozen more men he put the whole army to rout. Ling himself escaped.

sentences.zh: 進破高郵，引兵度淮，攻歷陽，據之，稱總管。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Gaoyou, led troops across the Huai, attacked Liyang, occupied it, and styled himself Chief Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to capture Gaoyou, led his army across the Huai, attacked Liyang, seized it, and styled himself Chief Commandant.

sentences.zh: 分兵徇屬縣，皆下，江淮群盜爭附。

translations.literal: He sent troops to subdue subject counties—all submitted—and the bandits of Jianghuai vied to attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched columns to bring the neighboring counties to heel, and all submitted. Bandits throughout the Jianghuai region scrambled to join him.

sentences.zh: 伏威選敢死士五千，號「上募」，寵厚之，與均甘苦，每攻取，必先登，戰罷，閱創在背者殺之。

translations.literal: Fuwei selected five thousand dare-to-die soldiers called "First Recruits," favored them generously, shared hardship with them equally; whenever he attacked he had to be first to climb; after battle he reviewed those wounded in the back and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei chose five thousand daredevils, called them the "First Recruits," and treated them with exceptional favor, sharing every hardship with them. In every assault he had to be the first man up the wall. After battle he inspected the wounded: anyone struck in the back was executed.

sentences.zh: 所虜獲必分與麾下，士有戰死，以其妻殉，故人自奮戰，無完敵。

translations.literal: Captured goods he always divided among his officers; if a soldier died in battle, his wife was buried with him; therefore men fought of themselves and there was no unbeaten foe.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever booty was taken he divided among his men. When a soldier fell in battle, his wife was buried with him. For this reason his followers fought with desperate courage, and his enemies were never left standing.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及以為歷陽太守，不受。

translations.literal: Yu Wen Huaji made him Administrator of Liyang but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenhuaji appointed him administrator of Liyang, but he refused the post.

sentences.zh: 徙丹陽，自稱大行臺。

translations.literal: He moved to Danyang and styled himself Grand Executive.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted his base to Danyang and styled himself Grand Executive.

sentences.zh: 始進用士人，繕利兵械，薄賦斂，除殉葬法，民奸若盜及吏受賕，雖輕，皆殺無赦。

translations.literal: He began employing scholars, repaired weapons, lightened taxes, abolished the law of burial with the dead; if the people were adulterers or thieves, or officials took bribes, even lightly, all were killed without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He began to employ men of learning, sharpened his armaments, and reduced taxes. He abolished the custom of burying the living with the dead. Adultery, theft, or official corruption—even in minor cases—was punished by death without mercy.

sentences.zh: 上表越王侗，侗以為東南道大總管，封楚王。

translations.literal: He memorialized King Yue Yang Tong; Yang Tong appointed him Grand Commander of the Southeastern Circuit and enfeoffed him as King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial to King Yue Yang Tong, who appointed him Grand Commander of the Southeastern Circuit and enfeoffed him as King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 是時，秦王方討王世充，遣使招懷，伏威乃獻款。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qin was attacking Wang Shichong and sent envoys to win him over; Fuwei thereupon submitted allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Qin was campaigning against Wang Shichong and sent envoys to win him over. Fuwei thereupon pledged his allegiance.

sentences.zh: 高祖授以東南道行臺尚書令、江淮安撫大使、上柱國、吳王，賜姓，豫屬籍，以其子德俊為山陽公，賜帛五千段，馬三百匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed him Southeastern Circuit Executive Secretariat Director, Grand Ambassador for Pacification of Jianghuai, Upper Pillar of State, King of Wu, granted the imperial surname, entered the register of imperial clan; his son Dejun was made Duke of Shanyang; five thousand bolts of silk and three hundred horses were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu appointed him Director of the Southeastern Circuit Executive Secretariat, Grand Ambassador for the Pacification of Jianghuai, Upper Pillar of State, and King of Wu; granted him the imperial surname and enrolled him in the imperial clan register. His son Dejun was made Duke of Shanyang, and he received five thousand bolts of silk and three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 伏威遣其將陳正通、徐紹宗以兵會，取世充之梁郡。

translations.literal: Fuwei sent his generals Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong with troops to join up and took Shichong's Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei sent his generals Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong with troops to join the campaign and captured Liang Prefecture from Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 又遣將王雄誕討李子通於杭州，禽以獻。

translations.literal: He also sent General Wang Xiongdan to attack Li Zitong at Hangzhou and captured him for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his general Wang Xiongdan to attack Li Zitong at Hangzhou and took him prisoner for presentation at court.

sentences.zh: 破汪華於歙州。

translations.literal: He defeated Wang Hua at Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Wang Hua at She Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 盡有江東、淮南地，南屬嶺，東至於海。

translations.literal: He fully possessed the lands of Jiangdong and Huainan, south to the ranges, east to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He came to hold all of Jiangdong and the Huai region, his domain reaching south to the mountain ranges and east to the sea.

sentences.zh: 秦王已平劉黑闥，師次曹、兗，伏威懼，乃入朝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin had pacified Liu Heidan; his army halted at Cao and Yan; Fuwei was afraid and entered court.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin had already pacified Liu Heidan and halted his army in Cao and Yan. Fuwei grew fearful and came to court in person.

sentences.zh: 詔拜太子太保兼行臺尚書令，留京師，位在齊王元吉上，以寵之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent concurrently Executive Secretariat Director, kept at the capital; his rank was above Prince Qi Li Yuanji, as a mark of favor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with concurrent duties as Director of the Executive Secretariat and kept him at the capital. His precedence was set above Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 伏威好神仙長年術，餌雲母被毒，武德七年二月，暴卒。

translations.literal: Fuwei loved the arts of immortals and longevity, swallowed mica and was poisoned; in the second month of the seventh year of Wude he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei was devoted to the arts of immortality and long life. He ingested mica and was poisoned by it. In the second month of the seventh year of Wude he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 初，公祏反，矯伏威令以紿眾，趙郡王孝恭既平公祏，得反書以聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gongshi rebelled he forged Fuwei's order to deceive the masses; Prince of Zhao Li Xiaogong after pacifying Gongshi obtained the rebel letters and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fu Gongshi rebelled, he forged orders in Fuwei's name to deceive the troops. After the Prince of Zhao Li Xiaogong had pacified Gongshi, he obtained the rebel correspondence and reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 高祖追其官，削屬籍，沒入家產。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu stripped his offices, removed him from the clan register, and confiscated family property.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu stripped him of his offices, removed his name from the imperial clan register, and confiscated his family property.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，太宗知其冤，詔復官爵，以公禮葬，仍還其子封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan Emperor Taizong knew he had been wronged, ordered restoration of office and titles, burial with due rites, and return of his son's fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan, Emperor Taizong, recognizing that he had been wronged, ordered his offices and titles restored, gave him burial with full honors, and returned his son's fief.

sentences.zh: 伏威有養子三十人，皆壯士，屬以兵，與同衣食，唯闞棱、王雄誕知名。

translations.literal: Fuwei had thirty adopted sons, all stalwart men; he entrusted them with troops and shared food and clothing with them; only Kan Ling and Wang Xiongdan were well known.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei had thirty adopted sons, all powerful warriors. He entrusted them with troops and shared food and clothing with them as with his own kin. Only Kan Ling and Wang Xiongdan were widely known.

sentences.zh: 闞棱，伏威邑人也。

translations.literal: Kan Ling was from Fuwei's home district.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ling was a fellow townsman of Fuwei.

sentences.zh: 貌魁雄，善用兩刃刀，其長丈，名曰「陌刀」，一揮殺數人，前無堅對。

translations.literal: His appearance was huge and heroic; he excelled with the double-edged blade; it was ten feet long and called "mo dao"; one swing killed several men; nothing strong stood before him.
translations.idiomatic: He was of towering, heroic build and excelled with the double-edged long sword. His blade was ten feet long and called the "mo dao." A single sweep could cut down several men at once, and no enemy formation could stand before him.

sentences.zh: 伏威據江淮，以戰功顯，署左將軍。

translations.literal: When Fuwei held Jianghuai, Ling distinguished himself in battle and was appointed Left General.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuwei held the Jianghuai region, Kan Ling distinguished himself in battle and was appointed Left General.

sentences.zh: 部兵皆群盜，橫相侵牟，棱案罪殺之，雖親故無脫者，至道不舉遺。

translations.literal: His troops were all band gangs who bullied one another; Ling judged crimes and executed them—even relatives did not escape; on the road nothing was left behind.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were former bandits who preyed on one another. Kan Ling tried them for their crimes and put them to death, sparing neither friend nor kin, until not even a scrap was left on the highway.

sentences.zh: 從伏威入朝，拜左領軍將軍、越州都督。

translations.literal: Following Fuwei to court he was appointed Left Defender General and Governor of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuwei came to court, Kan Ling accompanied him and was appointed Left Defender General and Governor of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 公祏反，棱與南討，青山之戰，與陳正通遇，陣方接，棱脫兜鍪謂眾曰：「不識我邪？

translations.literal: When Gongshi rebelled Ling went on the southern campaign; at the battle of Qingshan he met Chen Zhengtong; as the lines were about to engage Ling removed his helmet and told the crowd: "Do you not know me? How dare you fight!
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi rebelled, Kan Ling joined the southern campaign. At the battle of Qingshan he encountered Chen Zhengtong. As the two armies were about to clash, Kan Ling removed his helmet and shouted to the enemy ranks, "Do you not know who I am? How dare you fight me!

sentences.zh: 何敢戰！」

translations.literal: How dare you fight!
translations.idiomatic: How dare you fight me!

sentences.zh: 其徒多棱舊部，氣遂索，至有拜者。

translations.literal: His followers were mostly Ling's old troops; their spirit slackened; some even bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the enemy soldiers were Kan Ling's former comrades. Their fighting spirit collapsed, and some even bowed to him in greeting.

sentences.zh: 公祏破，棱功多，然頗自伐。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was broken Ling had great merit but was rather boastful.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi was defeated, Kan Ling won great distinction, yet he grew rather boastful of his achievements.

sentences.zh: 公祏被禽，乃誣與己謀；

translations.literal: When Gongshi was captured he framed him as having plotted with himself;
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi was captured, he falsely claimed that Kan Ling had conspired with him;

sentences.zh: 又伏威、王雄誕及棱貲產在丹陽者當原，而趙郡王孝恭悉籍入之，棱自訴，忤孝恭。

translations.literal: Also Fuwei, Wang Xiongdan and Ling had property at Danyang that should have been returned but Li Xiaogong registered everything; Ling appealed and offended Xiaogong.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, the property of Fuwei, Wang Xiongdan, and Kan Ling at Danyang ought to have been restored to them, but the Prince of Zhao Li Xiaogong had it all registered and confiscated. Kan Ling appealed on his own behalf and thereby offended Li Xiaogong.

sentences.zh: 遂以謀反誅。

translations.literal: He was therefore executed on charge of treason.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly executed on a charge of treason.

sentences.zh: 王雄誕，曹州濟陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Xiongdan was a native of Jiyin in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiongdan was a native of Jiyin in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 少強果，膂力絕人。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and resolute with matchless strength.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was fierce and resolute, with strength that none could match.

sentences.zh: 伏威之起，用其計，戰多克，署驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Fuwei rose he used his plans; in battles he often won and was appointed Flying Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuwei first rose in rebellion, Wang Xiongdan supplied his stratagems. He won battle after battle and was appointed Flying Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 初，伏威度淮與李子通合，後子通憚其才，襲之，伏威被創墮馬，雄誕負逃葭澤中，裒嘯散亡，又為隋將來整所窘，眾復潰。

translations.literal: At first when Fuwei crossed the Huai to join Li Zitong, later Zitong feared his ability and attacked him; Fuwei was wounded and fell from his horse; Xiongdan carried him fleeing into the reed marshes; gathered scattered troops; again was pressed by Sui general Lai Zheng; the army again collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Fuwei crossed the Huai to ally with Li Zitong, Zitong later grew afraid of his talent and turned on him. Fuwei was wounded and thrown from his horse. Wang Xiongdan carried him on his back into the reed marshes, gathered the scattered troops, and fought on—only to be cornered again by the Sui general Lai Zheng, whereupon the army collapsed once more.

sentences.zh: 別將西門君儀妻王勇決而力，負伏威走，雄誕總麾下壯士十余人從之。

translations.literal: Adjutant Ximen Junyi's wife Wang was resolute and strong; she carried Fuwei running; Xiongdan led more than ten stalwart followers.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of his officer Ximen Junyi, a woman named Wang, was bold and powerful. She hoisted Fuwei onto her back and ran. Wang Xiongdan rallied more than ten of his strongest warriors to follow.

sentences.zh: 追兵至，雄誕還拒，數被創，氣彌厲，伏威遂脫。

translations.literal: Pursuers arrived; Xiongdan turned back to resist, was wounded many times, spirit grew fiercer; Fuwei thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the pursuers caught up, Wang Xiongdan wheeled about to hold them off. He was wounded again and again, yet his fury only mounted. Fuwei thus made his escape.

sentences.zh: 闞棱年長於雄誕，故軍中號棱「大將軍」，雄誕「小將軍」。

translations.literal: Kan Ling was older than Xiongdan so in the army they called Ling "Great General" and Xiongdan "Little General."
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ling was older than Wang Xiongdan, so in the army they called Kan Ling the "Great General" and Wang Xiongdan the "Little General."

sentences.zh: 後伏威令輔公祏擊子通，以雄誕、棱為副，戰溧水，子通敗，公祏乘勝追之，反為所擠，士皆走壁。

translations.literal: Later Fuwei ordered Gongshi to attack Zitong with Xiongdan and Ling as deputies; they fought at Lishui; Zitong was defeated; Gongshi pursued with victory but was in turn pressed; soldiers all ran to the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fuwei ordered Fu Gongshi to attack Li Zitong, with Wang Xiongdan and Kan Ling as his deputies. They fought at Lishui. Li Zitong was defeated, and Fu Gongshi pressed the pursuit—but was in turn driven back, and his men fled to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 雄誕曰：「子通狃於勝，無營壘，今急擊之，必克。」

translations.literal: Xiongdan said: "Zitong is intoxicated with victory and has no camp stockade; if we strike urgently now we are sure to take him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiongdan said, "Li Zitong is drunk on his victory and has pitched no camp defenses. If we strike him now, hard and fast, he is sure to fall.

sentences.zh: 公祏不從。

translations.literal: Gongshi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gongshi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 雄誕獨提私卒數百，銜枚夜往，乘風火之，子通大敗走，度太湖。

translations.literal: Xiongdan alone led several hundred private soldiers, gagged mouths at night, came with wind and fire; Zitong was badly defeated and fled, crossing Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiongdan took several hundred of his own men, had them gag their mouths, and marched by night. He attacked with wind and fire. Li Zitong was routed and fled across Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，與子通戰蘇州，卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude he fought Zitong at Suzhou and repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude he fought Li Zitong at Suzhou and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 子通以精兵保獨松嶺，雄誕遣將陳當率千兵出不意，乘高蔽崦，張疑幟，夜縛炬於樹，遍山澤。

translations.literal: Zitong held elite troops at Dusong Ridge; Xiongdan sent Chen Dang with a thousand troops by surprise, high on the shaded cliff, many false banners; at night tied torches to trees across mountain and marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zitong held his crack troops on Dusong Ridge. Wang Xiongdan sent Chen Dang with a thousand men to take an unexpected route, stationing them high on the shaded slopes with many decoy banners. By night they bound torches to the trees until the hills and marshes blazed with light.

sentences.zh: 子通懼，燒營遁，保余杭，雄誕追禽之。

translations.literal: Zitong was afraid, burned camp and fled, held Yuhang; Xiongdan pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zitong was terrified, burned his camp, and fled to Yuhang. Wang Xiongdan pursued him and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 歙守汪華在郡稱王且十年，雄誕還師攻之，華以勁甲出新安洞拒戰，雄誕伏兵山谷，以弱卒數千鬥，輒走壁，華來攻，壁中奮殊死，不可下。

translations.literal: Shezhou defender Wang Hua had styled himself king in the commandery for nearly ten years; Xiongdan returned with troops to attack; Hua came out with strong armor through Xin'an Pass; Xiongdan hid troops in valleys, fought with weak soldiers of thousands, then fled to walls; when Hua came to attack, those in the walls fought desperately and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua, the defender of She Prefecture, had styled himself king in the region for nearly ten years. Wang Xiongdan turned back to attack him. Wang Hua marched out in heavy armor through Xin'an Pass. Wang Xiongdan hid troops in the valleys and met him with a few thousand weak soldiers, then feigned retreat to the walls. When Wang Hua pressed the attack, the defenders fought with desperate fury and the position could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 會暮還，雄誕伏兵已據洞口，不得歸，遽面縛降。

translations.literal: At dusk he returned; Xiongdan's ambush already held the pass mouth; could not return; hastily bound himself and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Wang Hua withdrew. Wang Xiongdan's ambush had already seized the mouth of the pass, cutting off his retreat. Wang Hua had no choice but to come forward bound and surrender.

sentences.zh: 蘇賊聞人遂安據昆山，無所屬，伏威使討之，雄誕以邑險而完，攻之引日，遂單騎造壘門，陳國威靈，因開曉禍福，遂安即降。

translations.literal: Suzhou bandit Wen Suian held Kunshan belonging to no one; Fuwei sent to attack; Xiongdan found the town steep and complete; attack drew out days; he alone rode to the camp gate, declared state prestige, opened persuasion of fortune and disaster; Suian at once submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Suian, a bandit of Suzhou, held Kunshan and acknowledged no master. Fuwei sent Wang Xiongdan against him. The stronghold was steep and well defended, and the siege dragged on for days. Wang Xiongdan then rode alone to the camp gate, proclaimed the majesty of the state, and laid out the consequences of resistance and submission. Wen Suian surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 以前後功授歙州總管，封宜春郡公。

translations.literal: For former and latter merit he was made Governor of Shezhou and Duke of Yichun.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated victories he was appointed Governor of She Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Yichun.

sentences.zh: 伏威入朝，以兵屬雄誕。

translations.literal: When Fuwei entered court he left his troops under Xiongdan.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuwei came to court he left his army under Wang Xiongdan's command.

sentences.zh: 輔公祏將反，患其異己，縱反間，陽言得伏威教，責雄誕貳。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was about to rebel he feared his dissent, spread false intelligence, openly claiming he had Fuwei's instruction, blaming Xiongdan's treachery.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi was plotting rebellion he feared Wang Xiongdan's independence. He spread false reports, openly claiming he had Fuwei's orders, and accused Wang Xiongdan of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 雄誕素質直，信之，乃歸臥疾。

translations.literal: Xiongdan was by nature straight and believed it; he returned and lay ill.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiongdan was by nature upright and trusting, and he believed the story. He returned to quarters and feigned illness.

sentences.zh: 公祏奪其兵，遣西門君儀諭計，雄誕始悔寤，曰：「天下方靖，王在京師，當謹守籓，奈何為族夷事？

translations.literal: Gongshi seized his troops and sent Ximen Junyi with the plan; Xiongdan first regretted and awakened saying: "All under Heaven is just pacified; the King is in the capital—should guard the frontier carefully—how undertake a matter that exterminates the clan?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gongshi stripped him of his command and sent Ximen Junyi to lay out the plot. Wang Xiongdan then came to his senses with regret and said, "The realm has only just been pacified. The King is in the capital. We ought to guard our post faithfully—how can we undertake an act that will destroy our whole clan?

sentences.zh: 雄誕雖死，誼不從！」

translations.literal: Though Xiongdan dies, righteousness he will not follow!
translations.idiomatic: Even if Wang Xiongdan must die, he will not follow you in treason!

sentences.zh: 公祏遂縊之。

translations.literal: Gongshi thereupon strangled him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gongshi thereupon had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 雄誕愛人，善撫士，能致下死力，每破城邑，整眾山立，無絲毫犯。

translations.literal: Xiongdan loved people and well comforted troops, could make subordinates die for him; whenever he took a city he arrayed troops standing like a mountain with not the slightest violation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiongdan cared for his men and knew how to win their loyalty so that they would die for him. Whenever he captured a city he held his troops in strict formation, and not the least disorder was permitted.

sentences.zh: 死之日，江南士庶為流涕。

translations.literal: On the day of his death gentry and commoners of Jiangnan wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his death, scholars and commoners throughout the Jiangnan region wept for him.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其節，以子世果襲宜春郡封。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu praised his integrity; his son Shiguo inherited the Yichun fief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu honored his loyalty. His son Shiguo inherited the fief of Yichun.

sentences.zh: 太宗立，優詔贈左驍衛大將軍、越州都督，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended an excellent edict posthumously granted Left Valiant Cavalry Grand General, Governor of Yuezhou, posthumous name Zhong (Loyal).
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, an edict of special favor posthumously appointed him Left Valiant Cavalry Grand General and Governor of Yuezhou, with the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 世果，垂拱初至廣州都督、安西大都護。

translations.literal: Shiguo, at the beginning of Chuigong reached Governor of Guangzhou and Grand Protector of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shiguo, at the beginning of the Chuigong era, rose to Governor of Guangzhou and Grand Protector of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 張士貴，虢州盧氏人，本名忽峍。

translations.literal: Zhang Shigui was a native of Lushi in Guozhou; his original name was Hula.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shigui was a native of Lushi in Guozhou. His original name was Hula.

sentences.zh: 彎弓百五十斤，左右射無空發。

translations.literal: He bent a bow of one hundred fifty jin; shooting left and right none missed.
translations.idiomatic: He could draw a bow of one hundred fifty jin and shoot to left or right without ever missing.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，起為盜，攻剽城邑，當時患之，號「忽峍賊」。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui Daye he rose as bandit attacking cities; people then feared him and called him "Hula Bandit."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, in the Daye era, he took to banditry and raided cities. The people feared him and called him the "Hula Bandit."

sentences.zh: 高祖移檄招之，士貴即降，拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu moved a proclamation to summon him; Shigui at once submitted, was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu issued a proclamation summoning him to submit. Zhang Shigui surrendered at once and was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendor.

sentences.zh: 從征伐有功，賜爵新野縣公。

translations.literal: Following campaigns he had merit, was enfeoffed Duke of Xinye county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the armies on campaign and won distinction, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 又從平洛，授虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Again following pacification of Luoyang he was made Governor of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the campaign to pacify Luoyang and was appointed Governor of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「顧令卿衣錦晝遊耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Intended to let you, sir, return home in brocade by day.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I meant for you to return home in glory, clad in brocade by daylight.

sentences.zh: 進封虢國公、右屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Advanced enfeoffment as Duke of Guo state, Right Defender of the Encampment Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was further enfeoffed as Duke of Guo and appointed Right Defender of the Encampment Grand General.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，為龔州道行軍總管，破反獠還，太宗聞其冒矢石先登，勞之曰：「嘗聞以忠報國者不顧身，於公見之。」

translations.literal: Seventh year Zhenguan, was Gongzhou circuit campaigning commander, broke rebellious Lao and returned; Taizong heard he braved arrows and stones first up, comforted him: "I have heard that those who repay the state with loyalty disregard their bodies—on you I see it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he served as commander of the Gongzhou circuit campaign, crushed the rebellious Lao tribes, and returned. Emperor Taizong heard that he had charged ahead through flying arrows and stones and comforted him, saying, "I have heard that those who repay the state with loyalty do not spare their own lives—and in you I see it.

sentences.zh: 累遷左領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Repeated promotion to Left Defender Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted, eventually reaching the post of Left Defender Grand General.

sentences.zh: 顯慶初，卒，贈荊州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Beginning of Xianqing he died; posthumously made Governor of Jingzhou, buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianqing era he died. He was posthumously appointed Governor of Jingzhou and buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 苑君璋，馬邑豪也，以趫雄自奮。

translations.literal: Yuan Junzhang was a magnate of Mayi; he exerted himself with fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Junzhang was a powerful local figure of Mayi who prided himself on his fierce courage.

sentences.zh: 劉武周以兵入寇，君璋曰：「唐以一州兵掇取三輔，所向風靡，此殆天命，非人謀，不可爭也。

translations.literal: When Liu Wuzhou invaded with troops Junzhang said: "Tang with one province's troops seized the three suburbs, wherever they went they swept all—this is likely Heaven's mandate, not human plan—cannot be contested.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou invaded with his army, Yuan Junzhang said, "Tang took the capital with the forces of a single province and swept all before them wherever they marched. This looks like Heaven's mandate, not mere human scheming. It cannot be opposed.

sentences.zh: 太原而南多巖阻，今束甲深入，無踵軍，有失不可償，不如連突厥與唐合從，南面稱孤，上策也。」

translations.literal: South of Taiyuan are many cliff barriers; now bundling armor deep inward with no following army—loss cannot be repaid—better join Turks with Tang in alliance, style oneself king on the south, supreme stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: South of Taiyuan the terrain is rugged and full of natural barriers. If we drive deep into enemy country without a reserve force behind us, a single defeat would be irreparable. Far better to ally with the Turks against Tang and proclaim ourselves kings in the south—that is the supreme strategy.

sentences.zh: 武周不聽，使君璋守朔州，引眾內侵，未幾敗，泣曰：「廢君言，乃至此！」

translations.literal: Wuzhou did not listen, made Junzhang guard Shuozhou, led the masses inward to invade; before long defeated, wept: "Having abandoned your words, we come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou would not heed him. He left Yuan Junzhang to guard Shuozhou and led his main force south to invade. Before long he was defeated. Weeping, he said, "I ignored your counsel, and now it has come to this!"

sentences.zh: 即與共趨突厥。

translations.literal: He then with him together hastened to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: He then fled with Yuan Junzhang to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 武周死，突厥以君璋為大行臺，統武周部曲，使郁射設監兵，與舊將高滿政夜襲代州，不克。

translations.literal: Wuzhou died; the Turks made Junzhang Grand Executive, commanding Wuzhou's former troops, sent Yay she with supervisory troops together with old general Gao Manzheng by night to surprise Dai Prefecture, did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Wuzhou died, the Turks appointed Yuan Junzhang Grand Executive, placing him in command of Wuzhou's former troops. They sent the Yay she to oversee his forces, and together with the old general Gao Manzheng he launched a night attack on Dai Prefecture, but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使招之，賜鐵券，約不死。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent envoys to summon him, granted iron certificate, covenant of no death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent envoys to summon him, granted him an iron certificate guaranteeing he would not be put to death, and pledged him immunity.

sentences.zh: 君璋拒命，進寇代州，刺史王孝德拒卻之。

translations.literal: Junzhang refused the command and advanced to raid Dai Prefecture; Prefect Wang Xiaode repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Junzhang refused to obey and marched against Dai Prefecture. The prefect Wang Xiaode drove him back.

sentences.zh: 滿政勸君璋曰：「夷狄無禮，豈可北面臣之？

translations.literal: Manzheng urged Junzhang: "The barbarians are without propriety—how can one face north and serve them as subject?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Manzheng urged Yuan Junzhang, saying, "The barbarians know no propriety. How can we bow north and serve them as subjects?

sentences.zh: 請盡殺其眾以歸唐。」

translations.literal: Please kill all their followers and return to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Let us slaughter their entire force and return to Tang.

sentences.zh: 君璋不從。

translations.literal: Junzhang did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Junzhang would not agree.

sentences.zh: 而馬邑困於兵，人厭亂，滿政因眾不忍，夜脅君璋，君璋奔突厥。

translations.literal: Mayi was weary of war; the people hated disorder; Manzheng used the masses' impatience, by night coerced Junzhang; Junzhang fled to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Mayi was ravaged by warfare and the people were sick of chaos. Gao Manzheng played on their discontent and by night forced Yuan Junzhang's hand. Junzhang fled to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 滿政以城歸，詔拜朔州總管，封榮國公。

translations.literal: Manzheng surrendered the city and returned; an edict appointed him Governor of Shuozhou and enfeoffed him as Duke of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Manzheng handed the city over to Tang. An edict appointed him Governor of Shuozhou and enfeoffed him as Duke of Rong.

sentences.zh: 君璋引突厥攻陷馬邑，殺滿政，夷其黨，乃去，退保恒安。

translations.literal: Junzhang led Turks to attack and take Mayi, killed Manzheng, exterminated his faction, then left and withdrew to guard Heng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Junzhang led the Turks to storm Mayi, killed Gao Manzheng, and wiped out his followers. He then withdrew to hold Heng'an.

sentences.zh: 其部皆中國人，多叛去，君璋窮，乃降，自請鄣虜贖罪。

translations.literal: His troops were mostly Chinese; many rebelled and left; Junzhang was destitute and then submitted, himself requesting to guard the frontier and atone for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his followers were Chinese subjects, and many deserted him. Reduced to desperation, Yuan Junzhang surrendered and asked to be posted on the frontier to redeem his crimes.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣雁門人元普賜金券，會頡利亦召之，意猶豫。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent Yuan Pu of Yanmen to bestow a gold certificate; at the same time Jieli also summoned him; he was still hesitant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent Yuan Pu of Yanmen to present a gold bond of safe conduct. At the same time Khan Jieli summoned him as well, and Yuan Junzhang wavered between the two.

sentences.zh: 子孝政諫曰：「大人許唐降，又貳頡利，自取亡也。

translations.literal: His son Xiaozheng remonstrated: "Father, you promised Tang you would submit, yet you waver toward Jieli—you invite your own destruction.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan Xiaozheng admonished him, saying, "Father, you pledged yourself to Tang, yet now you hedge toward Jieli. You are courting your own ruin.

sentences.zh: 今糧盡眾攜，不即決，恐衿肘變生，孝政不忍見禍之酷也！」

translations.literal: Now grain is exhausted and the masses are divided; if you do not decide at once, I fear trouble will arise at the elbow; Xiaozheng cannot bear to see such cruel disaster!
translations.idiomatic: Our provisions are gone and the men are falling away. If you do not act now, I fear disaster will strike at any moment. I cannot bear to watch such ruin overtake us!

sentences.zh: 即單騎南奔，君璋喻返之，召眾與議。

translations.literal: He alone rode south to flee; Junzhang sent word for him to return and summoned the assembly to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse south alone to defect. Yuan Junzhang sent after him and called the leaders together for counsel.

sentences.zh: 恒安人郭子威曰：「恒安故王者都，山川足以自固，突厥方強，我援之，可觀天下變，何遽降？」

translations.literal: Guo Ziwei of Heng'an said: "Heng'an was the capital of former kings; mountains and rivers suffice for self-defense; the Turks are just strong—we aid them and can watch changes in the realm—why submit in haste?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziwei of Heng'an said, "This was once a royal capital. The terrain is strong enough to hold. The Turks are at their height—we need only stand with them and watch how the empire turns. Why rush to surrender?

sentences.zh: 君璋然之，執元普送突厥，頡利德之，遣以錦裘羊馬。

translations.literal: Junzhang agreed, seized Yuan Pu and sent him to the Turks; Jieli was pleased and sent brocade robes, sheep, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Junzhang agreed, seized Yuan Pu, and handed him over to the Turks. Jieli was pleased and sent him brocade robes, sheep, and horses in reward.

sentences.zh: 其下怨，投書於門曰：「不早附唐，父子誅。」

translations.literal: His subordinates were resentful and posted a letter at the gate saying: "By not submitting to Tang early, father and son will be executed.
translations.idiomatic: His men grew resentful and nailed a placard to the gate: "Because you would not submit to Tang in time, father and son will be put to death.

sentences.zh: 孝政懼，欲自歸，為君璋所拘。

translations.literal: Xiaozheng was afraid and wished to surrender himself but was detained by Junzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiaozheng, in fear, tried to defect on his own but Yuan Junzhang had him detained.

sentences.zh: 與突厥寇馬邑，犯太原，邊人苦之。

translations.literal: With the Turks he raided Mayi and invaded Taiyuan; the border people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Turks in raiding Mayi and striking at Taiyuan, and the frontier people groaned under the devastation.

sentences.zh: 見頡利政亂，知將亡，遂率所部降，頡利追，擊走其兵。

translations.literal: Seeing Jieli's government in disorder and knowing he would perish, he then led his division to submit; Jieli pursued and struck away his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw that Jieli's rule was collapsing and knew the Turks were finished, he led his followers in surrender. Jieli pursued and routed his rear guard.

sentences.zh: 入朝，拜安州都督，封芮國公，食五百戶，賜帛四千匹。

translations.literal: He entered court; was appointed Governor of Anzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Rui, fief of five hundred households, granted four thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court and was appointed Governor of Anzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Rui with a fief of five hundred households, and granted four thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 君璋不曉書，然天資習事，歷職有惠稱。

translations.literal: Junzhang did not understand writing, yet by nature was practiced in affairs; in each post he had a reputation for kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Junzhang could not read, yet he had a natural knack for affairs of state, and in every office he won a reputation for fair dealing.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，卒。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Zhenguan reign.

sentences.zh: 羅藝，字子廷，襄州襄陽人，家京兆之雲陽。

translations.literal: Luo Yi, style Ziting, was a man of Xiangyang in Xiangzhou; his family was in Yunyang of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi, courtesy name Ziting, was a native of Xiangyang in Xiangzhou, though his family had settled in Yunyang in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 父榮，隋監門將軍。

translations.literal: His father Rong was a Sui Gate Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luo Rong had been a gate guard general of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 藝剛愎不仁，勇攻戰，善用槊。

translations.literal: Yi was obstinate and unkind, brave in attack and battle, excelled with the spear.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi was stubborn and harsh, fierce in battle, and a master of the spear.

sentences.zh: 大業中，以戰力補虎賁郎將。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was appointed Tiger Guard Lieutenant for martial valor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he was appointed a lieutenant of the Tiger Guard for his fighting prowess.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，李景以武衛大將軍督饟北平，詔藝以兵屬，分部嚴一。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign Li Jing as Grand General of the Martial Guard supervised supplies at Beiping; an edict ordered Yi's troops subordinate to him; divisions were strict and unified.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, Li Jing served as Grand General of the Martial Guard directing supplies at Beiping. An edict placed Luo Yi's troops under his command, and Yi enforced strict discipline throughout the ranks.

sentences.zh: 然任氣，嘗慢侮景，頻為景辱。

translations.literal: Yet he was willful and often insulted Jing lightly; repeatedly was humiliated by Jing.
translations.idiomatic: But he was proud and willful and often treated Li Jing with contempt, for which Li Jing repeatedly humiliated him.

sentences.zh: 天下盜起，涿郡號富饒，伐遼兵仗多在，而倉{廣寺}盈羨，又臨朔宮多珍寶，屯師且數萬，苦盜賊侵掠，留守將趙什住、賀蘭誼、晉文衍等不能支。

translations.literal: Bandits rose throughout the realm; Zhuo Commandery was called rich; the army's weapons for the Liaodong campaign were mostly there, and the granaries overflowed; also near Shuogong Palace were many treasures; troops stationed numbered tens of thousands; they suffered bandit raids; the garrison generals Zhao Shizhu, Helan Yi, Jin Wenyian and others could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion spread across the empire. Zhuo Commandery was famed for its wealth—the arms stockpiled for the Liaodong campaign lay there, and the granaries brimmed with grain. The nearby Shuogong Palace held treasures beyond count, and tens of thousands of troops were encamped in the region, yet they were harried by bandits. The garrison commanders Zhao Shizhu, Helan Yi, Jin Wenyian, and others could not cope.

sentences.zh: 藝捍寇，數破卻之，勇常冠軍，為諸將忌畏。

translations.literal: Yi defended against bandits, repeatedly defeated and repelled them; his courage often led the army; the generals envied and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi fought off the raiders again and again, his valor unmatched among the commanders. The other generals both envied and feared him.

sentences.zh: 藝陰自計，因出師，詭說眾曰：「吾軍討賊數有功，而食乏。

translations.literal: Yi secretly calculated; on going out with the army he deceived the masses saying: "Our army in attacking bandits has often had merit, yet we lack food.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi plotted in secret. On one campaign he deceived his men, saying, "We have won victory after victory against the bandits, yet we are starving.

sentences.zh: 官粟若山，而留守不賑恤，豈安人強眾意邪？」

translations.literal: Official grain is like a mountain, yet the garrison commanders will not relieve and comfort—is this the intent to secure the people and strengthen the host?
translations.idiomatic: The government granaries are piled like hills, yet the garrison commanders refuse to open them. Is this how they mean to keep the people safe and the army strong?

sentences.zh: 士皆怨。

translations.literal: The soldiers all resented.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were furious.

sentences.zh: 既還，郡丞出郊謁，藝執之，陳兵入，什住等懼，爭聽命。

translations.literal: On returning the commandery assistant went out to the suburbs to greet; Yi seized him, entered with troops displayed; Shizhu and others were afraid and vied to obey.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the assistant prefect came out to greet them. Luo Yi seized him, marched in with arms displayed, and Zhao Shizhu and the others, terrified, scrambled to obey his orders.

sentences.zh: 藝即發庫貲賜戰士，倉粟給窮人，境內大悅。

translations.literal: Yi at once opened the storehouses to reward warriors, gave granary grain to the poor; within the borders all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi opened the storehouses at once, rewarded his soldiers, and distributed grain to the destitute. The whole region erupted in joy.

sentences.zh: 殺異己者渤海太守唐祎等，威動北邊，柳城、懷遠並歸附。

translations.literal: He killed dissenters such as Bohai Prefect Tang Yi and others; his might shook the northern border; Liucheng and Huaiyuan both submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He killed those who opposed him, including Bohai Prefect Tang Yi. His power shook the northern frontier, and Liucheng and Huaiyuan both submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 黜柳城太守楊林甫，改郡曰營州，以襄平太守鄧皓為總管，藝自稱幽州總管。

translations.literal: He removed Liucheng Prefect Yang Linfu, changed the commandery name to Yingzhou, made Xiangping Prefect Deng Hao Chief Commandant; Yi styled himself Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He deposed Liucheng Prefect Yang Linfu, renamed the commandery Yingzhou, appointed Xiangping Prefect Deng Hao as chief commandant, and styled himself Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及至山東，遣使招藝，藝曰：「我隋舊臣，今大行顛覆，義不辱於賊。」

translations.literal: When Yu Wen Huaji reached Shandong he sent envoys to recruit Yi; Yi said: "I am an old minister of Sui; now the Great Line is overturned—I will not suffer disgrace from bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Wenhuaji reached Shandong he sent envoys to win Luo Yi over. Luo Yi replied, "I am a loyal servant of the Sui. The dynasty lies in ruins—I will not endure insult from a rebel.

sentences.zh: 斬使者，為煬帝發喪三日。

translations.literal: He beheaded the envoys and held mourning for Emperor Yang for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He executed the envoys and observed three days of mourning for Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 時竇建德、高開道亦遣使於藝，藝謂官屬曰：「建德等皆劇賊，不足共功名，唐公起兵據關中，民望所系，王業必成，吾決歸之。

translations.literal: At that time Dou Jiande and Gao Kaidao also sent envoys to Yi; Yi told his officials: "Jiande and the rest are fierce bandits, unworthy to share glory with; the Duke of Tang has risen holding Guanzhong, where the people's hopes lie—his royal enterprise is sure to succeed—I am resolved to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande and Gao Kaidao also sent envoys. Luo Yi told his staff, "Jiande and his ilk are nothing but fierce bandits, unfit to share in great deeds. The Duke of Tang has raised his banner in Guanzhong, where the people's hopes rest. His cause is certain to triumph. I have decided to join him.

sentences.zh: 敢異議者戮！」

translations.literal: Who dares dissent—execute!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever disagrees—off with his head!

sentences.zh: 會張道源撫輯山東，亦諭藝降，武德二年，乃奉表以地歸。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Daoyuan was pacifying Shandong and also urged Yi to submit; in the second year of Wude he then presented a memorial returning the land.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Daoyuan was then pacifying Shandong and likewise urged him to submit. In the second year of Wude, Luo Yi presented a memorial offering his territory to Tang.

sentences.zh: 詔封燕王，賜姓，豫屬籍。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed him King of Yan, granted surname, entered imperial clan register.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed him as King of Yan, granted him the imperial surname, and enrolled him in the clan register.

sentences.zh: 數與建德戰，多所禽馘。

translations.literal: He repeatedly fought Jiande and captured and beheaded many.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Dou Jiande repeatedly and took many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 秦王擊劉黑闥，高祖詔藝弟監門將軍壽以兵從，藝自率眾數萬破劉什善、張君立於徐河。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin attacked Liu Heidan; Emperor Gaozu ordered Yi's younger brother, Gate Guard General Shou, to follow with troops; Yi himself led tens of thousands and at Xu River defeated Liu Shishan and Zhang Junli.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin campaigned against Liu Heidan, Emperor Gaozu ordered Luo Yi's younger brother, gate guard general Luo Shou, to join the army. Luo Yi himself led tens of thousands of men and at the Xu River defeated Liu Shishan and Zhang Junli.

sentences.zh: 黑闥引突厥入寇，藝復以兵與皇太子建成會洺州，遂請入朝。

translations.literal: Heidan led Turks to invade; Yi again joined Crown Prince Li Jiancheng at Mingzhou with troops, then requested to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heidan brought the Turks in to raid, Luo Yi again marched with Crown Prince Li Jiancheng to Mingzhou. He then asked permission to come to court.

sentences.zh: 帝厚禮之，拜左翊衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor treated him generously and appointed Left Wing Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him with great honor and appointed him Left Wing Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 藝負其功，且貴重不少屈，秦王左右嘗至其營，藝{疒只}辱之。

translations.literal: Yi relied on his merit and was noble and important, seldom bending; the Prince of Qin's attendants once came to his camp and Yi insulted them.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi swaggered over his achievements and, proud of his rank, rarely humbled himself. When attendants of the Prince of Qin visited his camp, Luo Yi publicly humiliated them.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒，以屬吏，久乃釋。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was angry and handed him to the law officers; after a long time released him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was furious and turned him over to the judicial authorities. Only after a long interval was he released.

sentences.zh: 時突厥放橫，藉藝威名欲憚虜，詔以本官領天節軍將，鎮涇州。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks ran rampant; borrowing Yi's prestige to awe the barbarians, an edict had him in his former office lead the Tianjie Army General, garrisoning Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were then running wild on the frontier. The court hoped to use Luo Yi's name to intimidate them and ordered him, in his former rank, to command the Tianjie Army and garrison Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，進開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Luo Yi was promoted to Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.

sentences.zh: 藝內懼，乃圖反，詭言閱武。

translations.literal: Yi was inwardly afraid and then plotted rebellion, falsely announcing a review of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi was inwardly terrified and plotted rebellion, announcing under false pretenses that he would hold a military review.

sentences.zh: 兵既集，稱被密詔入朝，軍至豳，治中趙慈皓出謁，遂據州。

translations.literal: When troops were gathered he claimed to have a secret edict to enter court; the army reached Bin; Assistant Governor Zhao Cihao came out to greet; he then seized the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once the troops were assembled, he claimed he had received a secret edict summoning him to court and marched to Bin Prefecture. When Assistant Governor Zhao Cihao came out to greet him, Luo Yi seized the city.

sentences.zh: 帝命長孫無忌、尉遲敬德擊之，未至，慈皓與統軍楊岌謀誅藝，藝覺，執慈皓。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zhangsun Wuji and Yuchi Jingde to attack; before they arrived, Cihao with Commander Yang Ji plotted to kill Yi; Yi perceived it and seized Cihao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Zhangsun Wuji and Yuchi Jingde against him. Before they arrived, Zhao Cihao and the army commander Yang Ji plotted to assassinate Luo Yi. Luo Yi discovered the plot and seized Zhao Cihao.

sentences.zh: 岌居外，即攻之，藝敗，棄妻子，從數百騎奔突厥。

translations.literal: Ji was outside and at once attacked; Yi was defeated, abandoned wife and children, followed by several hundred horsemen fled to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji, stationed outside the city, attacked at once. Luo Yi was defeated. He abandoned his wife and children and fled to the Turks with only a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 抵寧州，騎稍亡，左右斬之，傳首，梟於都市。

translations.literal: Reaching Ningzhou, horsemen gradually deserted; his attendants beheaded him and sent the head; it was displayed in the capital market.
translations.idiomatic: At Ningzhou his followers dwindled away. His own men cut off his head and sent it in. It was displayed on the execution ground in the capital.

sentences.zh: 壽時為利州都督，亦及誅。

translations.literal: Shou was then Governor of Lizhou and was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Luo Shou, who was then Governor of Lizhou, was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 先是，濟陰女子李，自言通鬼道，能愈疾，四方惑之，詔取致京師。

translations.literal: Earlier, a woman of Jiyin surnamed Li claimed to communicate with ghosts and could cure illness; the four directions were deluded; an edict had her brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a woman of Jiyin surnamed Li had claimed to traffic with spirits and cure disease. People flocked to her from every direction until an edict summoned her to the capital.

sentences.zh: 嘗往來藝家，謂藝妻孟曰：「妃相貴，當母天下。」

translations.literal: She often came and went at Yi's house, telling Yi's wife Meng: "Consort, your physiognomy is noble—you will be mother of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: She frequented Luo Yi's household and told his wife Lady Meng, "Your features mark you for greatness. You are destined to be empress.

sentences.zh: 孟令視藝，又曰：「妃之貴由於王，貴色且發。」

translations.literal: Meng had her look at Yi; she again said: "The consort's nobility comes from the King; noble color is about to appear."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Meng had her read Luo Yi's face as well. The woman said, "Your ladyship's glory flows from your husband. The signs of greatness are already rising in him."

sentences.zh: 藝妻信之，亦贊以反，既敗，與李皆斬。

translations.literal: Yi's wife believed it and also urged rebellion; after defeat, she and Li were both beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi's wife believed her and urged her husband to rebel. After his defeat, both she and the woman Li were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 王君廓，并州石艾人。

translations.literal: Wang Junguo was a man of Shiai in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junguo was a native of Shiai in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，為駔儈，無行，善盜。

translations.literal: In youth orphaned and poor, he was a horse broker, without conduct, skilled at theft.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in his youth, he worked as a horse broker. He was a man of no principle and an accomplished thief.

sentences.zh: 嘗負竹笱如魚具，內置逆刺，見鬻繒者，以笱囊其頭，不可脫，乃奪繒去，而主不辨也，鄉里患之。

translations.literal: He once carried a bamboo basket like a fish trap with hidden spikes inside; seeing one selling silk, he covered his head with the basket so it could not be removed, then seized the silk and left while the owner could not identify him; the village suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: He once carried a bamboo fish basket lined with hidden spikes. Spotting a silk merchant, he dropped the basket over the man's head so that it could not be pulled off, then made off with the silk while the victim could not see who had robbed him. The neighborhood lived in dread of him.

sentences.zh: 大業末，欲聚兵為盜，請與叔俱，不從，乃誣鄰人通叔母者，與叔共殺之，遂皆亡命。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he wished to gather troops as bandits and asked his uncle to join; the uncle refused; he then falsely accused a neighbor of adultery with the uncle's wife and with the uncle together killed him, then both fled.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era he planned to raise a band of robbers and asked his uncle to join him. When the uncle refused, he falsely accused a neighbor of sleeping with his uncle's wife, persuaded his uncle to help kill the man, and then both fled into hiding.

sentences.zh: 眾稍集，掠夏、長平。

translations.literal: Followers gradually gathered; they plundered Xia and Changping.
translations.idiomatic: His following slowly grew, and they raided through Xia and Changping.

sentences.zh: 河東丞丁榮拒之，且遣使慰召。

translations.literal: Hedong Assistant Ding Rong resisted him and also sent envoys to comfort and summon.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Rong, assistant prefect of Hedong, resisted him but also sent envoys to win him over with promises.

sentences.zh: 君廓見使，謬為欲歸首者。

translations.literal: Junguo saw the envoy and falsely made as if wishing to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junguo received the envoy and pretended he wished to submit.

sentences.zh: 榮輕之，因陳兵登山，君廓悉伏甲山谷中。

translations.literal: Rong despised him and therefore arrayed troops climbing the mountain; Junguo hid armor throughout the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Rong underestimated him and marched his troops up the heights. Wang Junguo had armed men lying in wait throughout the valleys.

sentences.zh: 榮軍還，掩擊，破之。

translations.literal: When Rong's army returned he ambushed and struck, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Rong's force withdrew, Wang Junguo sprang the ambush and routed them.

sentences.zh: 又與賊韋寶、鄧豹等掠虞鄉，宋老生與戰，君廓不利，保方山，老生列營迫之。

translations.literal: Again with bandits Wei Bao, Deng Bao and others he plundered Yuxiang; Song Laosheng fought him; Junguo was disadvantaged, held Fangshan; Laosheng arrayed camps pressing him.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the bandits Wei Bao and Deng Bao in raiding Yuxiang. Song Laosheng gave battle. Wang Junguo was hard pressed and fell back to Mount Fang. Song Laosheng camped close around him.

sentences.zh: 君郭糧盡，詐請降，與老生隔澗語，祈請哀到。

translations.literal: Junguo's grain was exhausted; he falsely requested surrender and spoke with Laosheng across the stream, praying with grief reaching the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junguo's provisions ran out. He feigned a wish to surrender and called across the stream to Song Laosheng, pleading with such anguish that his voice broke.

sentences.zh: 老生為感動，稍緩之，君廓一昔遁去。

translations.literal: Laosheng was moved and slightly relaxed; Junguo in one night fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Song Laosheng was touched and eased his pressure. In a single night Wang Junguo slipped away.

sentences.zh: 高祖兵起，召之，不從。

translations.literal: When Gaozu's army rose he summoned him; he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu raised his army, he summoned Wang Junguo, who refused to come.

sentences.zh: 歸李密，密不甚禮，乃歸國。

translations.literal: He returned to Li Mi; Mi did not greatly honor him; he then returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: He went over to Li Mi, who treated him coldly, and then submitted to Tang.

sentences.zh: 授上柱國、假河內太守、常山郡公，遷遼州刺史，徙封上谷，從戰東都有功，為右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Appointed Upper Pillar of State, Acting Governor of Henei, Duke of Changshan, moved to Governor of Liaozhou, transferred enfeoffment to Shanggu, followed campaign at eastern capital with merit, made Right Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Upper Pillar of State, acting governor of Henei, and Duke of Changshan, then transferred to Governor of Liaozhou and re-enfeoffed in Shanggu. He followed the eastern capital campaign with distinction and was made Right Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 詔勞之曰：「爾以十三人破賊萬，自古以少制眾，無有也！」

translations.literal: An edict comforted him saying: "You with thirteen men broke ten thousand bandits—from antiquity using few to control many, there has been nothing like it!
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him: "You routed ten thousand rebels with thirteen men. Never in history has so small a force overcome so large.

sentences.zh: 賜雜彩百段。

translations.literal: Granted one hundred bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one hundred bolts of patterned silk.

sentences.zh: 別下軒轅、羅川二縣，破世充將魏隱，擊糧道緱氏，沈米艘三十柁。

translations.literal: Separately he descended Xuanyuan and Luochuan two counties, defeated Shichong's general Wei Yin, struck the grain route at Gongshi, sank thirty grain boats.
translations.idiomatic: He separately reduced Xuanyuan and Luochuan counties, defeated Wang Shichong's general Wei Yin, struck the grain route at Jian, and sank thirty supply barges.

sentences.zh: 進爵彭國公，鎮幽州。

translations.literal: Advanced enfeoffment Duke of Peng, garrisoned Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Duke of Peng and stationed at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 擊突厥，俘斬二千，獲馬五千匹。

translations.literal: He attacked the Turks, captured and beheaded two thousand, obtained five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the Turks, capturing and killing two thousand men and seizing five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 入朝，帝賜所乘馬，令自廷中乘以出，謂侍臣曰：「昔藺相如叱秦王，目眥皆烈。

translations.literal: He entered court; the Emperor bestowed the horse he himself rode, ordered him to mount from within the hall and ride out, telling attendants: "Formerly Lin Xiangru berated the King of Qin until his eyes bulged with rage.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court. The emperor gave him the horse he himself had been riding and told him to mount in the hall and ride out before the court. He said to his ministers, "Long ago Lin Xiangru faced down the King of Qin until his eyes blazed with fury.

sentences.zh: 君廓往擊建德，李勣遏之，至發憤大呼，鼻耳皆流血，其勇何特古人哉！

translations.literal: When Junguo went to strike Jiande, Li Ji restrained him; he even vented fury with a great shout, nose and ears all bleeding—how does his courage differ from men of old?
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Junguo fought Dou Jiande, Li Ji had to hold him back. He raged and shouted until blood ran from his nose and ears. What ancient hero matched such fury?

sentences.zh: 朕當不以例賞。」

translations.literal: I shall not reward him by the usual measure.
translations.idiomatic: I will not reward him by the ordinary standard.

sentences.zh: 乃賜錦袍金帶，還幽州。

translations.literal: He then granted brocade robe and gold belt and returned him to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He granted him a brocade robe and gold belt and sent him back to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 會大都督廬江王瑗反，欲奪君廓兵以委王詵。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Commander Prince of Lujiang Li Yuan rebelled and wished to seize Junguo's troops to entrust to Wang Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Commander, Prince of Lujiang Li Yuan, rebelled, he tried to strip Wang Junguo of his command and hand the troops to Wang Chen.

sentences.zh: 君廓本紿瑗使亂為己功，乃從數騎候詵，留騎於外，曰：「聞呼聲則入。」

translations.literal: Junguo had originally deceived Yuan to make disorder his own merit; he then followed with several horsemen to wait on Chen, leaving horsemen outside saying: "If you hear a shout, enter."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junguo had originally tricked Li Yuan into rebellion so that he might claim the credit for putting it down. He rode with a few followers to visit Wang Chen, leaving his men outside with orders to rush in at the sound of a cry."

sentences.zh: 乃獨款詵，詐曰：「有急變，當白！」

translations.literal: Hearing a shout then enter."
translations.idiomatic: At my shout, come in."

sentences.zh: 詵方沐，握發出，即斬之，因執瑗。

translations.literal: He alone approached Chen sincerely saying: "There is urgent change—must report!" Chen was bathing, grasped his hair and came out; at once beheaded him, then seized Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He entered alone and said urgently, "There is an emergency—I must report it!" Wang Chen was bathing. Wang Junguo seized him by the hair as he came out and cut off his head, then took Li Yuan prisoner.

sentences.zh: 以功授幽州都督，瑗家口悉賜之，進左光祿大夫，賜帛千段。

translations.literal: For merit appointed Governor of Youzhou; Yuan's household all bestowed on him; advanced Left Grand Master of Splendor, granted one thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he was appointed Governor of Youzhou. Li Yuan's entire household was given to him as slaves. He was promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendor and granted one thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 居職不守法度，長史李玄道數以法繩督，猜惑不自安。

translations.literal: In office he did not observe law; Chief Clerk Li Xuandao several times bound and supervised by law; he grew suspicious and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In office he scorned the law. His chief clerk Li Xuandao repeatedly held him to account. Wang Junguo grew suspicious and uneasy.

sentences.zh: 會被召，至渭南，殺驛史，亡奔突厥，野人斬之。

translations.literal: When summoned, reaching Weinan, he killed the relay clerk, fled to the Turks; wild men beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to court, he reached Weinan, murdered the post-station clerk, and fled toward the Turks. Frontier tribesmen cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 太宗顧前功，為收葬，待其家如初。

translations.literal: Taizong considering his former merit had him buried and treated his family as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, mindful of his past service, had him buried with honor and treated his family as before.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫溫彥博奏：「君廓叛臣，不宜食封邑，有司失所宜言。」

translations.literal: Censor Grandee Wen Yanbo memorialized: "Junguo was a rebel minister—he should not enjoy a fief; the officials lost what they ought to have said.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Wen Yanbo submitted: "Wang Junguo was a traitor. He ought not to retain his fief. The officials failed to speak as they should.

sentences.zh: 乃貶為庶人。

translations.literal: He was therefore degraded to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: His title was accordingly stripped and he was reduced to commoner status.
